messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug causing ClassUtils.getShortClassName() to improperly handle array class names is due to how the method processes class names of arrays. The failing test expects "String[]" as the short class name for a String array class, but the current implementation appends a semicolon instead, e.g., "String;".

The method ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?> cls) calls getShortClassName(cls.getName()), forwarding the array class name string. For an array, cls.getName() returns the binary name, which for example for a String array is "[Ljava.lang.String;". The method getShortClassName(String) then tries to parse this name to extract the short name.

Inside getShortClassName(String), it simply looks for the last dot ('.') and inner class separators ('$'), and returns the substring after the last dot, without array awareness. So for "[Ljava.lang.String;", the last dot is before "String;", so it returns "String;", which includes the trailing semicolon. This causes the incorrect output.

The underlying issue is that getShortClassName(String) does not sanitize or convert array binary names into their readable form before processing. The current functions point to getCanonicalName(String) (called by getShortCanonicalName) that deals with array notation by stripping leading "[" characters, replacing abbreviated codes with full class names, removing trailing semicolons and appending "[]" per dimension count. This logic correctly converts array class names to canonical names like "java.lang.String[]". However, getShortClassName(String) does not call getCanonicalName(String) and thus does not benefit from this array handling.

Therefore, the bug is that getShortClassName(String) does not handle array class names correctly. It treats them as normal class names, simply taking substrings which retain trailing semicolons and the encoded array format. It should instead reuse or integrate the logic from getCanonicalName(String) to convert array names to their canonical form before extracting the short class name.

# Methods to fix
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)  
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.Class<?>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
